arc-toolchain-n: Add headers from frameworks/native/vulkan Import the following headers: frameworks/native/vulkan/include/hardware/hwvulkan.h frameworks/native/vulkan/include/vulkan/vk_android_native_buffer.h frameworks/native/vulkan/include/vulkan/vk_layer_interface.h frameworks/native/vulkan/include/vulkan/vk_platform.h frameworks/native/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan.h frameworks/native/vulkan/include/vulkan/vulkan_loader_data.h These headers are needed, obviously, to enable Vulkan in ARC++. To minimize the risk in this change, I hand-rolled the new tarball. The new tar file does not contain a rebuild of the toolchain, as built by files/gather.py. Instead, I created the new tar file by unpacking the old one, then *appending* each desired header like so: $ gunzip arc-toolchain-n-2017.07.24.tar.gz $ cp arc-toolchain-n-2017.07.24.tar arc-toolchain-n-2017.08.30.tar $ mkdir stage $ pushd stage $ tar xf ../arc-toolchain-n-2017.08.30.tar $ rsync -r ~/android/frameworks/native/vulkan/include/ amd64/usr/include/ $ rsync -r ~/android/frameworks/native/vulkan/include/ arm/usr/include/ $ tar uvf ../arc-toolchain-n-2017.08.30.tar . ./arm/usr/include/vulkan/ ./arm/usr/include/vulkan/vk_android_native_buffer. ./arm/usr/include/vulkan/vk_layer_interface.h ./arm/usr/include/vulkan/vk_platform.h ./arm/usr/include/vulkan/vulkan.h ./arm/usr/include/vulkan/vulkan_loader_data.h ./arm/usr/include/hardware/hwvulkan.h ./amd64/usr/include/vulkan/ ./amd64/usr/include/vulkan/vk_android_native_buffe ./amd64/usr/include/vulkan/vk_layer_interface.h ./amd64/usr/include/vulkan/vk_platform.h ./amd64/usr/include/vulkan/vulkan.h ./amd64/usr/include/vulkan/vulkan_loader_data.h ./amd64/usr/include/hardware/hwvulkan.h $ popd $ gzip arc-toolchain-n-2017.08.30.tar BUG=b:36895696 TEST=$ sudo emerge arc-toolchain-n && find /opt/android-n | grep vulkan $ cbuildbot --remote --test-tryjob \ -p chromiumos/overlays/chromiumos-overlay \ caroline-release elm-release Change-Id: I703314f63cf32a997dad5744dee087ab45433d90 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/644355 Commit-Ready: Chad Versace <chadversary@chromium.org> Tested-by: Chad Versace <chadversary@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Luis Hector Chavez <lhchavez@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Tomasz Figa <tfiga@chromium.org>

pack_firmware: Show the model name in the versions file At present for shared firmware we list all the firmware versions but there is no indication of which model they are for. Previously this was obvious since it was part of the version name: BIOS version: Google_Reef.9042.50.0 With shared firmware, we can have a situation where all models use the same firmware and thus have the same line above. Add a new line which shows the model, so we have, for example: Model: reef BIOS image: 99a6fc64e45596aa2c1a9911cddce952 */models/reef/image.bin BIOS version: Google_Reef.9042.50.0 EC image: 60c08e5aefa3a660687c7027d1358df0 */models/reef/ec.bin EC version: reef_v1.1.5857-77f6ed7 Model: pyro BIOS image: 409974485838ed7beb199b42892ba948 */models/pyro/image.bin BIOS version: Google_Pyro.9042.41.0 EC image: 752de0224d5b3bae77d12534d3df8038 */models/pyro/ec.bin EC version: pyro_v1.1.5840-f0d7761 Model: electro BIOS image: 99a6fc64e45596aa2c1a9911cddce952 */models/reef/image.bin BIOS version: Google_Reef.9042.50.0 EC image: 60c08e5aefa3a660687c7027d1358df0 */models/reef/ec.bin EC version: reef_v1.1.5857-77f6ed7 Here, electro uses the reef firmware, but it is obvious that this is the case. init: Add scripts from Coral to all projects. There are two scripts we implemented for Coral and found it to be useful for all projects: - select_default_test_list: A script to select default test list if not defined yet. Its current implementation is based on "model" and only works on JSON test lists. - device_id/reset_test_results: Sometimes partner may try to clone (dd, or reading eMMC directly) a disk image from one golden device to another. Also there are devices with internal storage can be removed (for example old SSD via SATA) that partner will run test by connecting newly built motherboard with a "golden disk". The factory should detect both cases and reset test states. BUG=chromium:738969 TEST=None Change-Id: I9baa524a0366d9d4add8d0e9aedce84c587709a2 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/647065 Commit-Ready: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org> Tested-by: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org>

goofy.js: Refactor tab UI. Refactor tab UI and extract everything that are related to another file, so it's easier to add support for other UI layout. Also refactor the logic of visible test. The old logic was that goofy backend is the root of trust for which test is visible, and there's only one visible test at a time. The new logic is that the UI manager is the root of trust for which test is visible, and there may be multiple tests that are visible at a time. (For preparation of upcoming tiled UI feature.) BUG=b:64963909 TEST=make test TEST=manually on DUT. Fix issue with upgrade running when not needed If a touch event was generated while the application was running it could be interpreted as a result of a I/O command. If that happened when reading current firmware version, a new upgrade would be triggered even if it was running the latest version. This made the touch unresponsive for up to a minute. Fix the issue by only accepting io responses with HID report id 10. BUG=b:65224683 TEST=Ran using udev-rule and manually with --recovery both with touching and without touching the display. Change-Id: I6eb1a2286944fd85d1f1763c7d2e716a1f204cae Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/645811 Commit-Ready: Stefan Adolfsson <sadolfsson@chromium.org> Tested-by: Zhongze Hu <frankhu@google.com> Reviewed-by: Zhongze Hu <frankhu@google.com>

chromeos-base: Move pkg_postinst to pkg_preinst. When pkg_postinst fails, portage doesn't know that anything went wrong and proceeds, but this leaves the SDK in a non-functioning state. Move the logic into pkg_preinst where failures will be treated as a merge failure. This would have caught things like crbug.com/757147 much sooner.
